question: Can we design a xenobot that sweeps loose particles into a pile?

generations.asked: the donor organism, as the nearest thing the layers can represent
a 0.5-1 mm ciliated construct swimming at 0.1-0.5 mm/s
the task: sweeping loose particles into piles
could it exist anywhere outside a dish

0.asked: the donor organism, as the nearest thing the layers can represent

frame.name: construct
frame.label: a construct: cells assembled into a shape the donor organism never makes
frame.why: base.made_from is set: a construct has no body plan to inherit, so its shape is declared rather than looked up
frame.silhouette: a spheroid with one ciliated face; the shape is the design, so it is declared per run and carries no donor anatomy

axes.x: anterior (+) to posterior (-), normalised to the body's own length
axes.z: right (+) to left (-); a slot with side "paired" is instantiated at +z and -z
axes.units: body lengths, so a frame is scale-free

frame.THIS_IS_NOT_MORPHOMETRY: Every position here is DECLARED by this file, not measured from any specimen and not derived from any ontology. A slot says 'the eye goes near the front of the head, on both sides'; it does not say how big a fly's eye is or where it sits in millimetres. The only morphometric geometry in this repository is anatomy-model/parametric, which builds one teleost from Park and Choi's measurements. Nothing here should ever be read off as a measurement, and the theatre view labels every part with this basis.

source.title: A two-step mechanism generates the spacing pattern of the ciliated cells in the skin of Xenopus embryos.

chain_links.quote: This choice is under the control of lateral inhibition mediated by a Suppressor of Hairless-dependent Notch signaling pathway, in which X-Delta-1 is the putative ligand driving the selection process
chain_links.what_it_does_not_show: the abstract itself calls X-Delta-1 the 'putative' ligand; only the Su(H)-dependence of the pathway is asserted, and no binding or reporter data are visible from the abstract. Nothing here is about a xenobot.

downgraded_by_verification.why: The quote hedges the very molecule that is this link's `from` node: X-Delta-1 is called the 'putative' ligand. No binding, reporter, epistasis or rescue result appears in the quote (abstract only), so the quote PROPOSES a pathway step rather than showing one. Per AGENT_BRIEF.md that is `hypothesis`, not `mechanism`.

source.title: A two-step mechanism generates the spacing pattern of the ciliated cells in the skin of Xenopus embryos.

chain_links.quote: Because nascent ciliated-cell precursors prevent neighboring cells from taking on the same fate, a scattered pattern of these precursors is generated within the deep layer of the non-neural ectoderm.
chain_links.what_it_does_not_show: it gives no number: not how many multiciliated cells result, nor what fraction of the surface they cover, and nothing about a reassembled spheroid rather than an intact embryo.

chain_links.quote: skin, is known to be restricted by Notch signaling
chain_links.what_it_does_not_show: this quote is the fragment that survives the article's inline italic markup around 'Xenopus'; it carries the restriction of multiciliated-cell formation by Notch in Xenopus skin as prior work the paper cites, and the paper's own contribution is that mcidas is among the genes repressed by Notch. It is not a promoter-level demonstration.

downgraded_by_verification.why: The quote does not mention mcidas/MCI at all, and in context (PMC3329891.xml, first sentence of Results) it is a background citation to refs 10-13 - 'is known to be restricted by Notch signaling' - not a result of this paper. The paper's own mcidas-repressed-by-Notch finding sits in the NEXT, unquoted sentence. What the quote shows is a relation asserted from prior work, i.e. `hypothesis`.

chain_links.experiment_type: microinjection of 370 pg Notch ICD mRNA at the four-cell stage, then trajectory tracking of the resulting deciliated organisms
chain_links.stage: injected at the four-cell stage; organisms imaged after reaggregation

source.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
source.title: A scalable pipeline for designing reconfigurable organisms

chain_links.quote: the multiciliated cell inhibitor Notch ICD
chain_links.what_it_does_not_show: this is a methods label resting on cited prior work: the paper reports no multiciliated-cell count, cilia stain or beat measurement in the injected organisms. The grade rests on the paper then calling these organisms 'deciliated' and using them precisely to remove ciliary propulsion. Note also that this is the OPPOSITE of the design requirement - it removes ciliary locomotion rather than tuning it up.

downgraded_by_verification.why: The quote is a four-word methods label, 'the multiciliated cell inhibitor Notch ICD'. It reports no loss-of-function measurement whatever: no multiciliated-cell count, no cilia stain, no beat or speed measurement in the injected organisms, as the link's own `what_it_does_not_show` already concedes. A reagent name asserted from cited prior work is `hypothesis`, not `necessity`.

blueprint-well-formedness.label: An emitted anatomical blueprint graph is well-formed under its own rules
blueprint-well-formedness.about: the part graph itself: that each term is a node, each parent relation is one Uberon or CL relation, and the graph has no cycle
blueprint-well-formedness.how: Structural only. It certifies that the blueprint is a well-formed graph over ontology terms — it says nothing about whether the part could exist, work, or bear a load. It is the one law in the set that reaches every part of every organism, and the weakest thing anyone could want to know about any of them.

thompson1917-ch03-07.label: Weight tends to vary as the cube of linear dimensions during growth
thompson1917-ch03-07.about: the slope of log mass against log length is 3 under isometry
thompson1917-ch03-07.how: The cube law as an exponent, which makes it testable: a measured slope that is not 3 is a measurement of how the organism departs from isometry. E1 is the observation that this project's fish do depart.

altitude-coupling.label: Demand rises and supply falls with height together, so the flyable heights reach down to the ground
altitude-coupling.about: that the feasible set is downward closed in altitude: feasible high implies feasible low
altitude-coupling.how: Couples the two layers: thinner air both reduces lift and reduces oxygen, so a design feasible at altitude is feasible below it. Useful mainly as a sanity direction on a scenario sweep.

physiology-q10.label: Q10 temperature scaling: the ratio between two temperatures is Q10 raised to their difference over ten
physiology-q10.about: how a rate changes with a ten-degree change in temperature
physiology-q10.how: Proved, no instance: no candidate commits a Q10 and the conditions file fixes 25 C. Every rate in every run is therefore at one temperature, and a design whose selling point is a rate should say which temperature it means.

genotype-developmental-ordering.label: No structure develops from a precursor that appears later than it does
genotype-developmental-ordering.about: that a claimed developmental ordering has no cycle and respects the dependencies declared for it
genotype-developmental-ordering.how: The only law in the set that is about TIME, which makes it the one the time-lapse rests on. It certifies that an ordering is consistent; it does not supply one, does not predict a rate, and says nothing about how long a stage takes. A developmental animation is therefore a declared ordering being checked for consistency, never a simulation of development.

E2.label: The fitted mass exponent lies in [2.90, 3.02]
E2.about: a measured band for the weight ratio
E2.how: A measured band from one species. Outside that species it is a number, not a constraint.

E7.label: A lever lethal before the scoring stage cannot produce the phenotype
E7.about: that a trait appearing after a lethal stage cannot be scored
E7.how: The other law about time, and the one that matters most for a time-lapse: a part that appears after the organism would have died is not a part. Pairs with the developmental ordering law.

aerobic-power-bound.label: Sustained mechanical power is bounded by oxygen delivery (Fick) times efficiency
aerobic-power-bound.about: sustained flight requires aerobic supply at least the required mechanical power over the efficiency
aerobic-power-bound.how: The law that separates a glide from flight. A lifting surface large enough to hold the animal up says nothing about whether the animal can keep it up, and this is the only law in the set that asks. It takes Fick's principle as a NAMED HYPOTHESIS (fick_aerobic_supply) rather than proving it.

physiology-laplace.label: Laplace wall stress: pressure in a thin-walled vessel is limited by wall strength, thickness and radius
physiology-laplace.about: the pressure a thin-walled tube or sphere can hold, from radius, wall thickness and wall strength
physiology-laplace.how: Proved, with NO INSTANCE anywhere in this project: no vessel radius, wall thickness or wall strength exists for any organism here. It is in this table so that a part it would constrain carries the chip that says which three numbers are missing — a law with no instance is a request for data, and silence about it is worse.

muscle-power-premise.label: Thompson's muscle-power premise P = f p M (retired)
muscle-power-premise.how: STATED, NOT PROVED: a named hypothesis (MusclePowerLaw in lean/Delphi/Scaling.lean), replaced for the Studio by the aerobic bound. A chip for it must read as an assumption, because that is all it is.

fick-principle.label: Fick principle: aerobic supply is at most eta E Q (Ca - Cv)
fick-principle.about: oxygen delivery as flow times the arteriovenous difference
fick-principle.how: STATED, NOT PROVED: the aerobic bound takes it as its named hypothesis fick_aerobic_supply. Everything the aerobic bound concludes rests on it.

E3.label: Efficiency and O2 delivery lie in the ranges the cited sources support (widened after measured zebrafish)
E3.about: a measured ceiling on aerobic power
E3.how: The empirical input the aerobic bound needs. Measured in fish; borrowing it for an insect or a mammal is exactly the move the clade-scoped tables forbid.

E4.label: Gills do not ventilate in air
E4.about: a measured ceiling on stored (anaerobic) power
E4.how: The burst counterpart of E3: what a muscle can give for a few seconds. For a glide launch this is often the quantity that matters and the one least often declared.

scaling-strength-law.label: Strength scales as L^2: the missing half of Galileo's square-cube argument (R7)
scaling-strength-law.about: breaking load under isometry: it scales as L squared while weight scales as L cubed
scaling-strength-law.how: The reason a design cannot simply be made bigger. Weight grows faster than the cross-section carrying it, so a part that holds at one size fails at another with no change in material or shape.

elastic-similarity.label: Elastic similarity scaling (not formalised)
elastic-similarity.about: scaling that holds elastic deflection constant instead of stress
elastic-similarity.how: NOT FORMALISED. The named alternative to isometry for real skeletons, so its absence is why every scaling chip here says `under isometry`.

taxiing-thrust.label: Taxiing thrust on the water surface (not formalised)
taxiing-thrust.about: thrust produced while still in contact with the water
taxiing-thrust.how: NOT FORMALISED. The flying-fish runs needed it and did without it.

scaling-area-law.label: Area law and wing loading under isometry (R2, R3)
scaling-area-law.about: area under isometry: A scales as L squared
scaling-area-law.how: If the design scales a lifting or exchange surface by changing a length, this fixes the area ratio it gets — under isometry, which is a hypothesis about the design, not a fact about the animal. The flying-fish audit returns `violated` here for skin and fins, because that fish is NOT isometric: the law is right and the hypothesis is false, which is the useful outcome.

E1.label: Isometry fails within a species
E1.about: that measured fin area does not scale isometrically
E1.how: An OBSERVATION of Cypselurus hiraii, not a law. It is the evidence that the isometry hypothesis in the scaling laws is false for that fish, which is why those chips come back `violated` on that body.

genotype-pleiotropy-closure.label: An edit to a gene must be shown changing every node the map links that gene to
genotype-pleiotropy-closure.about: what a view of a genotype may omit: that the set shown is closed under the declared pleiotropy relation
genotype-pleiotropy-closure.how: A statement about the COMPLETENESS OF A VIEW, not about development. If a molecule is shown as affecting one part, this is what certifies that its other declared effects were not quietly dropped from the picture — which is exactly the failure a per-part panel invites.

genotype-genetic-code.label: A claimed amino-acid change is impossible below the code distance
genotype-genetic-code.about: what a claimed set of substitutions rules out, given the genetic code
genotype-genetic-code.how: Operates on a claimed edit. For a construct with an unedited donor genome there is nothing for it to operate on, and that is the honest answer rather than a refusal.

gene-regulatory-dynamics.label: Gene regulatory dynamics (not formalised)
gene-regulatory-dynamics.about: the dynamics of a regulatory network
gene-regulatory-dynamics.how: NOT FORMALISED, and it is the hole the whole scale ladder sits over. Nothing in the Lean set connects a molecule to a tissue. The ladder's molecular rungs are therefore LITERATURE, graded and quoted, and the theatre must never draw them in the same colour as a proof.

universal_laws.because: the quantities are there and no check in this run evaluated this law against them

missing_rungs.why: A xenobot has no organ. Kriegman et al. 2020 say so of their own constructs: 'above the cellular level, they bear little resemblance to existing organs or organisms' (runs/_chains/raw/xenobot/PMC6994979.xml, byte-exact). Links l12 and l13 therefore step straight from tissue to phenotype with skipped_rung set to 'organ'.
missing_rungs.what_would_be_needed: Nothing can close this one by experiment: the rung does not exist in this organism. A viewer that insists on an organ layer should render it as explicitly empty rather than invent one.

missing_rungs.why: No document fetched in this run gives a xenobot locomotion speed in any unit, so the requirement's 0.5-1 mm/s figure is unsourced as far as this ladder is concerned. The paper that reports ciliary xenobot locomotion quantitatively, Blackiston et al. 2021 Science Robotics, is not open access: its abstract was readable through PubMed, but Europe PMC returned HTTP 404 for its full text because it has no PMCID.
missing_rungs.what_would_be_needed: The full text or supplementary movies of Blackiston et al. 2021 (doi 10.1126/scirobotics.abf1571), or any tracked-trajectory dataset of ciliated xenobots with a calibrated scale bar and frame rate.

missing_rungs.why: Nothing fetched links a MEASURED multiciliated-cell density or coverage on a xenobot to that xenobot's measured speed or to how many particles it moves. Boselli et al. 2021 model coverage against transport on a flat Xenopus epidermis; Kriegman et al. 2021 observe locomotion and piling on a spheroid; no document connects the two quantities in the same specimen.
missing_rungs.what_would_be_needed: Per-xenobot multiciliated-cell counts (acetylated-tubulin staining, say) paired with tracked speed and a per-organism count of particles displaced, across a range of Notch-ICD doses.

missing_rungs.why: There is no genotype variable in this organism at all: the donor genome is unedited. The only molecular handles found in anything fetched here are an injected mRNA (Notch ICD, l14, which REMOVES ciliary locomotion) and a drug (WNT3A, l15, in a different Xenopus species and in an intact embryo). No document shows any molecular manipulation that INCREASES xenobot speed or improves particle sweeping.
missing_rungs.what_would_be_needed: A xenobot built from cells injected with mcidas or foxj1 mRNA (to raise multiciliated-cell number), or treated with WNT3A, with speed and particle sweeping measured against uninjected controls in the same dish.

missing_rungs.what_would_be_needed: An in situ or scRNA-seq census of a mature xenobot for small-secretory-cell markers. The Lee et al. 2023 animal-cap organoid atlas is the closest available dataset and does profile ionocytes and goblet cells, but the xenobot itself was not checked here.

verification.stance: Every claim was re-derived from the bytes. Quote matching was done by script, not by eye.

method.quote_matching: Python: each `quote` normalised to single spaces and searched in (a) the raw file, (b) the file with XML tags deleted (zero-width tag boundary), (c) the file with tags replaced by a space. A quote counted as verified only on a literal substring hit.
method.fetch_log: Each distinct `quote_from` path matched against runs/_chains/log/xenobot.fetch.json by `saved_to`, status asserted 200, and the file's sha256 recomputed and compared with the logged digest.
method.citation_identity: The pmid and doi claimed in each link's `source` compared with the pmid and doi recorded inside the fetched document.
method.grades: Each `evidence_grade` re-read against the five definitions in genotype/AGENT_BRIEF.md, judged strictly on what the QUOTE shows, not on what the paper as a whole probably shows.
method.holdout: Scanned for the names and terms of the held-out clade; no source from it was used in any link, quote or evidence field. The scan itself is in the fetch log and the verifier's scripts, not restated here.
method.identifiers: All 32 logged URLs parsed: hosts, query-parameter names, plus a regex scan of the entire log for email addresses, personal names, account ids, api keys and NCBI tool=/email= parameters.

checks.body: the blueprint comes back for Xenopus laevis: 13 organ systems, 67 organs, 214 tissues, 259 cell types. Every term is correct and the whole thing is about the wrong subject. That is a frog. A xenobot has no organ systems, no heart, no gut and no nervous system; it is a ball of skin and heart cells with cilia on the outside. The anatomy layer can describe the DONOR and has no way to express "an assembly of cells from this donor, in an arrangement the donor never makes".

numbers.the_gap: There is no construct layer. The blueprint vocabulary is taxon -> organ system -> organ -> tissue -> cell, and a xenobot is a cell-level assembly with nothing above it. Uberon has no term for it because it is not anatomy, and asking for one would be asking the ontology to describe an object that did not exist when it was written.

checks.body: the document now says what the subject IS: a construct made from Xenopus laevis, inheriting 3 things and explicitly not inheriting 5. base.taxon still carries the DONOR, because the cells really are that taxon and the genome is unedited, so sequence questions stay answerable; everything organismal does not, and the tools that cannot tell the difference now refuse instead of answering about a frog.

numbers.caveat: This document describes a CONSTRUCT: an assembly made FROM a taxon, which is not an instance of that taxon. The distinction is the whole point of the field. A xenobot is built from Xenopus laevis cells and is not a frog: it has no organ systems, no gut, no gonads and a working life of days, and the donor's anatomy, life history, ecology and predators are facts about the donor and not about it. base.taxon still carries the DONOR, because the cells really are that taxon and the genome really is unedited, so genotype questions are answerable; everything organismal is not. Any tool that reads a taxon from this document must say which of the two it is answering about, and the ones that cannot tell the difference refuse.

THE ONTOLOGY BARELY PLACES THIS BODY IN THIS ORGANISM. Of 727 parts the blueprint returned, 162 have an in_taxon restriction specific enough to be evidence that Xenopus laevis has them; 71 are restricted only to a clade containing most of the animal kingdom, and 494 carry no restriction at all. The blueprint keeps a part unless a constraint removes it, so most of what is drawn here is unevidenced rather than wrong.
No part in this view has measured geometry. Every position is a declared slot in sim-engine/scales/body-frames.json, and a shape is a primitive, not a morphology.

taxon_audit.headline: Of 727 parts: 162 placed specifically, 71 placed only vacuously, 494 unconstrained, 0 contested, 0 forbidden. Only the first number is evidence that a part belongs in Xenopus laevis.
taxon_audit.what_it_shows: Taxon constraints cannot do the work the blueprint layer asks of them. The blueprint keeps a part unless a constraint removes it, and for the great majority of parts the ontology either says nothing at all or says only that the part occurs somewhere in a clade containing most of the animal kingdom. That is why a fruit fly came back with bone marrow and a preen gland and without a brain: nothing in the pipeline was ever in a position to object.

lands_on.label: skin epidermis

chain_links.experiment_type: in situ / gain- and loss-of-function RNA injection (abstract)
chain_links.stage: embryo skin, before and during intercalation (stages not given in the abstract)

source.title: A two-step mechanism generates the spacing pattern of the ciliated cells in the skin of Xenopus embryos.

chain_links.quote: This choice is under the control of lateral inhibition mediated by a Suppressor of Hairless-dependent Notch signaling pathway, in which X-Delta-1 is the putative ligand driving the selection process
chain_links.what_it_does_not_show: the abstract itself calls X-Delta-1 the 'putative' ligand; only the Su(H)-dependence of the pathway is asserted, and no binding or reporter data are visible from the abstract. Nothing here is about a xenobot.

downgraded_by_verification.why: The quote hedges the very molecule that is this link's `from` node: X-Delta-1 is called the 'putative' ligand. No binding, reporter, epistasis or rescue result appears in the quote (abstract only), so the quote PROPOSES a pathway step rather than showing one. Per AGENT_BRIEF.md that is `hypothesis`, not `mechanism`.

to.label: Notch/Delta lateral inhibition between neighbouring non-neural ectoderm progenitors, selecting a scattered subset as multiciliated-cell precursors

lands_on.label: skin epidermis
lands_on.note: paper says 'deep layer of the non-neural ectoderm'

chain_links.experiment_type: lateral-inhibition assay by RNA injection, in situ (abstract)
chain_links.stage: non-neural ectoderm of the embryo, prior to radial intercalation

source.title: A two-step mechanism generates the spacing pattern of the ciliated cells in the skin of Xenopus embryos.

chain_links.quote: Because nascent ciliated-cell precursors prevent neighboring cells from taking on the same fate, a scattered pattern of these precursors is generated within the deep layer of the non-neural ectoderm.
chain_links.what_it_does_not_show: it gives no number: not how many multiciliated cells result, nor what fraction of the surface they cover, and nothing about a reassembled spheroid rather than an intact embryo.

to.label: Multicilin (mcidas), Xenopus laevis

lands_on.label: skin epidermis
lands_on.note: the experiment is on isolated Xenopus embryonic skin

chain_links.experiment_type: expression profiling of isolated skin after manipulating Notch activity
chain_links.stage: embryonic Xenopus skin

source.title: Multicilin promotes centriole assembly and ciliogenesis during multiciliate cell differentiation

chain_links.quote: skin, is known to be restricted by Notch signaling
chain_links.what_it_does_not_show: this quote is the fragment that survives the article's inline italic markup around 'Xenopus'; it carries the restriction of multiciliated-cell formation by Notch in Xenopus skin as prior work the paper cites, and the paper's own contribution is that mcidas is among the genes repressed by Notch. It is not a promoter-level demonstration.

downgraded_by_verification.why: The quote does not mention mcidas/MCI at all, and in context (PMC3329891.xml, first sentence of Results) it is a background citation to refs 10-13 - 'is known to be restricted by Notch signaling' - not a result of this paper. The paper's own mcidas-repressed-by-Notch finding sits in the NEXT, unquoted sentence. What the quote shows is a relation asserted from prior work, i.e. `hypothesis`.

chain_links.stage: tailbud stages

source.title: Fluid Mechanics of Mosaic Ciliated Tissues

chain_links.quote: The results presented here show that long-range hydrodynamic interactions between multiciliated cells allow efficient periciliary transport at low coverage, favoring coexistence of multiple cell types.
chain_links.what_it_does_not_show: the optimality claim is a model result, not a manipulation: nobody changed multiciliated-cell coverage and re-measured transport, which is why this is graded hypothesis. It also says nothing about a closed spheroid, where the surrounding fluid geometry differs from a flat epidermis.

source.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
source.title: A scalable pipeline for designing reconfigurable organisms

chain_links.quote: the multiciliated cell inhibitor Notch ICD
chain_links.what_it_does_not_show: this is a methods label resting on cited prior work: the paper reports no multiciliated-cell count, cilia stain or beat measurement in the injected organisms. The grade rests on the paper then calling these organisms 'deciliated' and using them precisely to remove ciliary propulsion. Note also that this is the OPPOSITE of the design requirement - it removes ciliary locomotion rather than tuning it up.

downgraded_by_verification.why: The quote is a four-word methods label, 'the multiciliated cell inhibitor Notch ICD'. It reports no loss-of-function measurement whatever: no multiciliated-cell count, no cilia stain, no beat or speed measurement in the injected organisms, as the link's own `what_it_does_not_show` already concedes. A reagent name asserted from cited prior work is `hypothesis`, not `necessity`.

parts.label: animal cap
parts.matched_by: label pattern /animal cap/ on "animal cap" (from the literature chain, not the blueprint)
parts.why: The literature chain names this anatomy, and the blueprint for Xenopus laevis (donor) does not contain it. It is drawn from the frame slot so the chain stays clickable; nothing in the phenotype layer asserts this part exists in the design.

laws.because: scope.taxa is [Danio rerio], and Xenopus laevis (donor) is in none of them. Its numbers are another clade's.
the organism document carries no genotype_edits

gene-regulatory-dynamics is proposed: there is no theorem to evaluate. NOT FORMALISED, and it is the hole the whole scale ladder sits over. Nothing in the Lean set connects a molecule to a tissue. The ladder's molecular rungs are therefore LITERATURE, graded and quoted, and the theatre must never draw them in the same colour as a proof.

to.label: multiciliated epithelial cell

lands_on.label: animal cap
lands_on.note: this is the exact tissue a xenobot is built from - a cultured animal-cap explant, not an intact embryo

chain_links.organism_of_evidence: Xenopus laevis (animal cap organoid, ex vivo)
chain_links.experiment_type: scRNA-seq with pseudotime lineage inference, validated by single-cell in situ HCR
chain_links.stage: Nieuwkoop and Faber stages 8 to 27; mcidas first seen at stage 13

source.title: A single-cell, time-resolved profiling of Xenopus mucociliary epithelium reveals nonhierarchical model of development

chain_links.quote: the multiciliated transcriptional program was initiated directly from the pluripotent tissue as a distinct lineage
chain_links.what_it_does_not_show: expression and pseudotime only - no perturbation in the organoid, so this link cannot carry necessity or sufficiency. It is the strongest evidence in this ladder that the fate programme runs in explanted cells, but it measures no cilia-driven flow.

blueprint-well-formedness.label: An emitted anatomical blueprint graph is well-formed under its own rules
blueprint-well-formedness.about: the part graph itself: that each term is a node, each parent relation is one Uberon or CL relation, and the graph has no cycle
blueprint-well-formedness.how: Structural only. It certifies that the blueprint is a well-formed graph over ontology terms — it says nothing about whether the part could exist, work, or bear a load. It is the one law in the set that reaches every part of every organism, and the weakest thing anyone could want to know about any of them.

thompson1917-ch03-07.label: Weight tends to vary as the cube of linear dimensions during growth
thompson1917-ch03-07.about: the slope of log mass against log length is 3 under isometry
thompson1917-ch03-07.how: The cube law as an exponent, which makes it testable: a measured slope that is not 3 is a measurement of how the organism departs from isometry. E1 is the observation that this project's fish do depart.

altitude-coupling.label: Demand rises and supply falls with height together, so the flyable heights reach down to the ground
altitude-coupling.about: that the feasible set is downward closed in altitude: feasible high implies feasible low
altitude-coupling.how: Couples the two layers: thinner air both reduces lift and reduces oxygen, so a design feasible at altitude is feasible below it. Useful mainly as a sanity direction on a scenario sweep.

physiology-q10.label: Q10 temperature scaling: the ratio between two temperatures is Q10 raised to their difference over ten
physiology-q10.about: how a rate changes with a ten-degree change in temperature
physiology-q10.how: Proved, no instance: no candidate commits a Q10 and the conditions file fixes 25 C. Every rate in every run is therefore at one temperature, and a design whose selling point is a rate should say which temperature it means.

genotype-developmental-ordering.label: No structure develops from a precursor that appears later than it does
genotype-developmental-ordering.about: that a claimed developmental ordering has no cycle and respects the dependencies declared for it
genotype-developmental-ordering.how: The only law in the set that is about TIME, which makes it the one the time-lapse rests on. It certifies that an ordering is consistent; it does not supply one, does not predict a rate, and says nothing about how long a stage takes. A developmental animation is therefore a declared ordering being checked for consistency, never a simulation of development.

E2.label: The fitted mass exponent lies in [2.90, 3.02]
E2.about: a measured band for the weight ratio
E2.how: A measured band from one species. Outside that species it is a number, not a constraint.

E7.label: A lever lethal before the scoring stage cannot produce the phenotype
E7.about: that a trait appearing after a lethal stage cannot be scored
E7.how: The other law about time, and the one that matters most for a time-lapse: a part that appears after the organism would have died is not a part. Pairs with the developmental ordering law.

aerobic-power-bound.label: Sustained mechanical power is bounded by oxygen delivery (Fick) times efficiency
aerobic-power-bound.about: sustained flight requires aerobic supply at least the required mechanical power over the efficiency
aerobic-power-bound.how: The law that separates a glide from flight. A lifting surface large enough to hold the animal up says nothing about whether the animal can keep it up, and this is the only law in the set that asks. It takes Fick's principle as a NAMED HYPOTHESIS (fick_aerobic_supply) rather than proving it.

physiology-laplace.label: Laplace wall stress: pressure in a thin-walled vessel is limited by wall strength, thickness and radius
physiology-laplace.about: the pressure a thin-walled tube or sphere can hold, from radius, wall thickness and wall strength
physiology-laplace.how: Proved, with NO INSTANCE anywhere in this project: no vessel radius, wall thickness or wall strength exists for any organism here. It is in this table so that a part it would constrain carries the chip that says which three numbers are missing — a law with no instance is a request for data, and silence about it is worse.

muscle-power-premise.label: Thompson's muscle-power premise P = f p M (retired)
muscle-power-premise.how: STATED, NOT PROVED: a named hypothesis (MusclePowerLaw in lean/Delphi/Scaling.lean), replaced for the Studio by the aerobic bound. A chip for it must read as an assumption, because that is all it is.

fick-principle.label: Fick principle: aerobic supply is at most eta E Q (Ca - Cv)
fick-principle.about: oxygen delivery as flow times the arteriovenous difference
fick-principle.how: STATED, NOT PROVED: the aerobic bound takes it as its named hypothesis fick_aerobic_supply. Everything the aerobic bound concludes rests on it.

E3.label: Efficiency and O2 delivery lie in the ranges the cited sources support (widened after measured zebrafish)
E3.about: a measured ceiling on aerobic power
E3.how: The empirical input the aerobic bound needs. Measured in fish; borrowing it for an insect or a mammal is exactly the move the clade-scoped tables forbid.

E4.label: Gills do not ventilate in air
E4.about: a measured ceiling on stored (anaerobic) power
E4.how: The burst counterpart of E3: what a muscle can give for a few seconds. For a glide launch this is often the quantity that matters and the one least often declared.

scaling-strength-law.label: Strength scales as L^2: the missing half of Galileo's square-cube argument (R7)
scaling-strength-law.about: breaking load under isometry: it scales as L squared while weight scales as L cubed
scaling-strength-law.how: The reason a design cannot simply be made bigger. Weight grows faster than the cross-section carrying it, so a part that holds at one size fails at another with no change in material or shape.

elastic-similarity.label: Elastic similarity scaling (not formalised)
elastic-similarity.about: scaling that holds elastic deflection constant instead of stress
elastic-similarity.how: NOT FORMALISED. The named alternative to isometry for real skeletons, so its absence is why every scaling chip here says `under isometry`.

taxiing-thrust.label: Taxiing thrust on the water surface (not formalised)
taxiing-thrust.about: thrust produced while still in contact with the water
taxiing-thrust.how: NOT FORMALISED. The flying-fish runs needed it and did without it.

scaling-area-law.label: Area law and wing loading under isometry (R2, R3)
scaling-area-law.about: area under isometry: A scales as L squared
scaling-area-law.how: If the design scales a lifting or exchange surface by changing a length, this fixes the area ratio it gets — under isometry, which is a hypothesis about the design, not a fact about the animal. The flying-fish audit returns `violated` here for skin and fins, because that fish is NOT isometric: the law is right and the hypothesis is false, which is the useful outcome.

E1.label: Isometry fails within a species
E1.about: that measured fin area does not scale isometrically
E1.how: An OBSERVATION of Cypselurus hiraii, not a law. It is the evidence that the isometry hypothesis in the scaling laws is false for that fish, which is why those chips come back `violated` on that body.

genotype-pleiotropy-closure.label: An edit to a gene must be shown changing every node the map links that gene to
genotype-pleiotropy-closure.about: what a view of a genotype may omit: that the set shown is closed under the declared pleiotropy relation
genotype-pleiotropy-closure.how: A statement about the COMPLETENESS OF A VIEW, not about development. If a molecule is shown as affecting one part, this is what certifies that its other declared effects were not quietly dropped from the picture — which is exactly the failure a per-part panel invites.

genotype-genetic-code.label: A claimed amino-acid change is impossible below the code distance
genotype-genetic-code.about: what a claimed set of substitutions rules out, given the genetic code
genotype-genetic-code.how: Operates on a claimed edit. For a construct with an unedited donor genome there is nothing for it to operate on, and that is the honest answer rather than a refusal.

gene-regulatory-dynamics.label: Gene regulatory dynamics (not formalised)
gene-regulatory-dynamics.about: the dynamics of a regulatory network
gene-regulatory-dynamics.how: NOT FORMALISED, and it is the hole the whole scale ladder sits over. Nothing in the Lean set connects a molecule to a tissue. The ladder's molecular rungs are therefore LITERATURE, graded and quoted, and the theatre must never draw them in the same colour as a proof.

missing_rungs.why: A xenobot has no organ. Kriegman et al. 2020 say so of their own constructs: 'above the cellular level, they bear little resemblance to existing organs or organisms' (runs/_chains/raw/xenobot/PMC6994979.xml, byte-exact). Links l12 and l13 therefore step straight from tissue to phenotype with skipped_rung set to 'organ'.
missing_rungs.what_would_be_needed: Nothing can close this one by experiment: the rung does not exist in this organism. A viewer that insists on an organ layer should render it as explicitly empty rather than invent one.

missing_rungs.why: No document fetched in this run gives a xenobot locomotion speed in any unit, so the requirement's 0.5-1 mm/s figure is unsourced as far as this ladder is concerned. The paper that reports ciliary xenobot locomotion quantitatively, Blackiston et al. 2021 Science Robotics, is not open access: its abstract was readable through PubMed, but Europe PMC returned HTTP 404 for its full text because it has no PMCID.
missing_rungs.what_would_be_needed: The full text or supplementary movies of Blackiston et al. 2021 (doi 10.1126/scirobotics.abf1571), or any tracked-trajectory dataset of ciliated xenobots with a calibrated scale bar and frame rate.

missing_rungs.why: Nothing fetched links a MEASURED multiciliated-cell density or coverage on a xenobot to that xenobot's measured speed or to how many particles it moves. Boselli et al. 2021 model coverage against transport on a flat Xenopus epidermis; Kriegman et al. 2021 observe locomotion and piling on a spheroid; no document connects the two quantities in the same specimen.
missing_rungs.what_would_be_needed: Per-xenobot multiciliated-cell counts (acetylated-tubulin staining, say) paired with tracked speed and a per-organism count of particles displaced, across a range of Notch-ICD doses.

missing_rungs.why: There is no genotype variable in this organism at all: the donor genome is unedited. The only molecular handles found in anything fetched here are an injected mRNA (Notch ICD, l14, which REMOVES ciliary locomotion) and a drug (WNT3A, l15, in a different Xenopus species and in an intact embryo). No document shows any molecular manipulation that INCREASES xenobot speed or improves particle sweeping.
missing_rungs.what_would_be_needed: A xenobot built from cells injected with mcidas or foxj1 mRNA (to raise multiciliated-cell number), or treated with WNT3A, with speed and particle sweeping measured against uninjected controls in the same dish.

missing_rungs.why: The serotonin/Htr3 beat-frequency loop (l09, l10) was shown in tadpole skin. Nothing fetched shows that small secretory cells exist in a xenobot at all, so it is unknown whether this control loop is present in the construct.
missing_rungs.what_would_be_needed: An in situ or scRNA-seq census of a mature xenobot for small-secretory-cell markers. The Lee et al. 2023 animal-cap organoid atlas is the closest available dataset and does profile ionocytes and goblet cells, but the xenobot itself was not checked here.

missing_rungs.why: ADDED BY VERIFICATION. l03 is the only link joining the Notch/Delta lateral-inhibition arm (l01, l02) to the multicilin arm (l04-l07), and its quote does not name mcidas and is a background citation rather than a result of the paper it is drawn from (see l03.downgraded_by_verification). With l03 at hypothesis grade, the two molecular arms of this ladder are not experimentally joined by anything fetched here: there is no quoted evidence that Notch represses mcidas specifically.
missing_rungs.what_would_be_needed: A quotable result sentence or figure legend from Stubbs et al. 2012 or a successor showing mcidas transcript or reporter levels rising when Notch activity is lowered and falling when it is raised, in the same experiment.

missing_rungs.why: ADDED BY VERIFICATION. A specimen break, distinct from the quantitative gap already logged between cell_cell and tissue. Every link from molecule through cell_cell (l01-l10) is evidenced in an intact Xenopus embryo or in an animal-cap explant; the only links whose organism_of_evidence is a xenobot are l11, l12, l13 - all `association`, all purely observational - and l14, now `hypothesis`. So no fetched document shows ANY of the Notch, multicilin or serotonin steps actually operating inside a reassembled spheroid: the mechanistic upper half of the ladder and the xenobot phenotype are joined by inference, not by a shared specimen.
missing_rungs.what_would_be_needed: In situ, immunostaining or scRNA-seq on mature xenobots for X-Delta-1/Notch targets, mcidas, foxj1 and acetylated tubulin, showing the same programme runs in the construct; ideally with a Notch-ICD dose series scored in the spheroid itself.

verification.stance: Every claim was re-derived from the bytes. Quote matching was done by script, not by eye.

method.quote_matching: Python: each `quote` normalised to single spaces and searched in (a) the raw file, (b) the file with XML tags deleted (zero-width tag boundary), (c) the file with tags replaced by a space. A quote counted as verified only on a literal substring hit.
method.fetch_log: Each distinct `quote_from` path matched against runs/_chains/log/xenobot.fetch.json by `saved_to`, status asserted 200, and the file's sha256 recomputed and compared with the logged digest.
method.citation_identity: The pmid and doi claimed in each link's `source` compared with the pmid and doi recorded inside the fetched document.
method.grades: Each `evidence_grade` re-read against the five definitions in genotype/AGENT_BRIEF.md, judged strictly on what the QUOTE shows, not on what the paper as a whole probably shows.
method.holdout: Scanned for the names and terms of the held-out clade; no source from it was used in any link, quote or evidence field. The scan itself is in the fetch log and the verifier's scripts, not restated here.
method.identifiers: All 32 logged URLs parsed: hosts, query-parameter names, plus a regex scan of the entire log for email addresses, personal names, account ids, api keys and NCBI tool=/email= parameters.

results.quote_match_modes: all 15 matched in the raw bytes after whitespace collapsing alone; none needed tag stripping

missing_rungs[tissue,organ], 'above the cellular level, they bear little resemblance...' - verified in PMC6994979.xml

The one non-200 call in the log, HTTP 404 for the Blackiston et al. full text, is already disclosed in refused_sources, and nothing was quoted from it beyond the PubMed abstract that was separately fetched.

results.walkable: The ladder IS walkable end to end as topology: molecule->pathway (l04 necessity, l05 mechanism), pathway->cell (l06 sufficiency), cell->cell_cell (l09 necessity), cell_cell->tissue (l10 necessity, l08 hypothesis), then tissue->phenotype directly (l12, l13 association) because the organ rung does not exist in this organism. Two of the three downgrades, l01 and l03, fall on the Notch/Delta arm, which is a parallel entry into the pathway rung, so none of them severs the walkable path. The path is nonetheless carried across its final step by `association`-grade observation only, and its mechanistic rungs come from a different specimen than its phenotype rungs - see the two missing_rungs added by this verification.
missing_rungs_added_detail: pathway<->molecule: the Notch->mcidas junction is unevidenced by its own quote
cell<->tissue: specimen break - no fetched document shows the mechanistic rungs operating inside a xenobot
results.holdout: Scanned for the names and terms of the held-out clade; no source from it was used in any link, quote or evidence field. The scan itself is in the fetch log and the verifier's scripts, not restated here.
results.identifier_leak: NONE. 32 logged URLs across 4 hosts (www.ebi.ac.uk, eutils.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov, rest.uniprot.org, ubergraph.apps.renci.org); query parameters are only db, fields, format, id, pageSize, query, resultType, retmode, rettype, size. No email address, personal name, account id, api key, or NCBI tool=/email= parameter anywhere in the log.

verification.not_changed: No link was deleted, no link was added, nothing was re-fetched, no existing missing_rungs entry was softened or removed, and the design_note - including its statement that there is no genotype variable in this organism - was left as written, because it is correct and the verifier found nothing in the fetched documents that contradicts it.

checks.about: whether the declared gait moves the body at all
checks.body: nothing this layer can check contradicts the design. That is NOT a finding that it moves: there is no muscle here, no metabolism, no control and no energy budget, and 1 of the 3 checks are regime indicators that never fail anything. Re is of order 5.0e-1, which the convention in media.json puts inside the creeping regime, though at the very top of it where inertia is beginning to matter. The asymmetry between the power and recovery strokes is exactly what the theorem requires: two paths, not one path retraced. That asymmetry is the reason cilia are shaped the way they are, and it is a property of the GAIT, which no part list contains.

theorem.reading: the stroke is declared non-reciprocal (4 degrees of freedom), so the theorem does not forbid it at any Reynolds number.

checks.body: the same construct with a single-hinge flap instead of cilia: impossible. IMPOSSIBLE, by a theorem and not by a simulation: the stroke is time-reversible (declared reciprocal) and Re <= 0.498 everywhere in the stated ranges. In the Stokes limit the displacement over a cycle depends on the PATH through configuration space and not on the rate, so a path that retraces itself returns the body exactly where it started. Net displacement per cycle is zero, at any beat frequency. This is the control for the check above -- a layer that returned "fine" for both would not be telling us anything about either.

order_of_appearance.why: Nothing in sim-engine or the Lean law set predicts when a part appears. genotype-developmental-ordering certifies that a DECLARED ordering has no cycle; E7 says a trait appearing after a lethal stage cannot be scored. Neither supplies an order.
order_of_appearance.what_would_be_needed: a staged expression or morphology dataset for the organism, and a rule mapping a stage to a part. For every organism in these runs that dataset does not exist.

timeline.not_a_simulation: This is a declared growth track being drawn, not development being simulated. No cell divides, no tissue forms and nothing moves; the body is redrawn larger.

2 part(s) are named by the literature chain and ABSENT from the blueprint (multiciliated epithelial cell, animal cap). They are drawn as ghosts, marked blueprint_has_it: false. For the fruit fly these are the very organs the longevity experiments act in.
The 13 molecules are marker annotations from the Protein Ontology, carried by the blueprint. None of them was measured in this organism and none is evidence of function.

The molecular rungs are LITERATURE in Xenopus laevis, Xenopus tropicalis, each link graded and quoted. Every link below comes from Xenopus laevis (in one case Xenopus tropicalis) embryos, from animal-cap organoids, or from published xenobots built out of unedited X. laevis cells; the taxon id NCBITaxon_8355 names the DONOR species, because a xenobot has no taxon of its own and no edited genome.

Rung tissue -> organ is MISSING: A xenobot has no organ. Kriegman et al. 2020 say so of their own constructs: 'above the cellular level, they bear little resemblance to existing organs or organisms' (runs/_chains/raw/xenobot/PMC6994979.xml, byte-exact). Links l12 and l13 therefore step straight from tissue to phenotype with skipped_rung set to 'organ'.

Rung tissue -> phenotype is MISSING: No document fetched in this run gives a xenobot locomotion speed in any unit, so the requirement's 0.5-1 mm/s figure is unsourced as far as this ladder is concerned. The paper that reports ciliary xenobot locomotion quantitatively, Blackiston et al. 2021 Science Robotics, is not open access: its abstract was readable through PubMed, but Europe PMC returned HTTP 404 for its full text because it has no PMCID.

Rung cell_cell -> tissue is MISSING: Nothing fetched links a MEASURED multiciliated-cell density or coverage on a xenobot to that xenobot's measured speed or to how many particles it moves. Boselli et al. 2021 model coverage against transport on a flat Xenopus epidermis; Kriegman et al. 2021 observe locomotion and piling on a spheroid; no document connects the two quantities in the same specimen.

Rung molecule -> phenotype is MISSING: There is no genotype variable in this organism at all: the donor genome is unedited. The only molecular handles found in anything fetched here are an injected mRNA (Notch ICD, l14, which REMOVES ciliary locomotion) and a drug (WNT3A, l15, in a different Xenopus species and in an intact embryo). No document shows any molecular manipulation that INCREASES xenobot speed or improves particle sweeping.

Rung cell -> cell_cell is MISSING: The serotonin/Htr3 beat-frequency loop (l09, l10) was shown in tadpole skin. Nothing fetched shows that small secretory cells exist in a xenobot at all, so it is unknown whether this control loop is present in the construct.

Rung pathway -> molecule is MISSING: ADDED BY VERIFICATION. l03 is the only link joining the Notch/Delta lateral-inhibition arm (l01, l02) to the multicilin arm (l04-l07), and its quote does not name mcidas and is a background citation rather than a result of the paper it is drawn from (see l03.downgraded_by_verification). With l03 at hypothesis grade, the two molecular arms of this ladder are not experimentally joined by anything fetched here: there is no quoted evidence that Notch represses mcidas specifically.

Rung cell -> tissue is MISSING: ADDED BY VERIFICATION. A specimen break, distinct from the quantitative gap already logged between cell_cell and tissue. Every link from molecule through cell_cell (l01-l10) is evidenced in an intact Xenopus embryo or in an animal-cap explant; the only links whose organism_of_evidence is a xenobot are l11, l12, l13 - all `association`, all purely observational - and l14, now `hypothesis`. So no fetched document shows ANY of the Notch, multicilin or serotonin steps actually operating inside a reassembled spheroid: the mechanistic upper half of the ladder and the xenobot phenotype are joined by inference, not by a shared specimen.
171 law chips are out of scope for this organism: the law is about the right quantity and its numbers belong to another clade.

THE ONTOLOGY BARELY PLACES THIS BODY IN THIS ORGANISM. Of 727 parts the blueprint returned, 0 have an in_taxon restriction specific enough to be evidence that Xenopus laevis (donor) has them; 0 are restricted only to a clade containing most of the animal kingdom, and 494 carry no restriction at all. The blueprint keeps a part unless a constraint removes it, so most of what is drawn here is unevidenced rather than wrong.
No part in this view has measured geometry. Every position is a declared slot in sim-engine/scales/body-frames.json, and a shape is a primitive, not a morphology.

taxon_audit.headline: Of 727 parts: 162 placed specifically, 71 placed only vacuously, 494 unconstrained, 0 contested, 0 forbidden. Only the first number is evidence that a part belongs in Xenopus laevis.
taxon_audit.what_it_shows: Taxon constraints cannot do the work the blueprint layer asks of them. The blueprint keeps a part unless a constraint removes it, and for the great majority of parts the ontology either says nothing at all or says only that the part occurs somewhere in a clade containing most of the animal kingdom. That is why a fruit fly came back with bone marrow and a preen gland and without a brain: nothing in the pipeline was ever in a position to object.

frame.THIS_IS_NOT_MORPHOMETRY: Every position here is DECLARED by this file, not measured from any specimen and not derived from any ontology. Nothing here should ever be read off as a measurement, and the theatre view labels every part with this basis.

chain_links.experiment_type: in situ / gain- and loss-of-function RNA injection (abstract)
chain_links.stage: embryo skin, before and during intercalation (stages not given in the abstract)

source.title: A two-step mechanism generates the spacing pattern of the ciliated cells in the skin of Xenopus embryos.

chain_links.quote: This choice is under the control of lateral inhibition mediated by a Suppressor of Hairless-dependent Notch signaling pathway, in which X-Delta-1 is the putative ligand driving the selection process
chain_links.what_it_does_not_show: the abstract itself calls X-Delta-1 the 'putative' ligand; only the Su(H)-dependence of the pathway is asserted, and no binding or reporter data are visible from the abstract. Nothing here is about a xenobot.

downgraded_by_verification.why: The quote hedges the very molecule that is this link's `from` node: X-Delta-1 is called the 'putative' ligand. No binding, reporter, epistasis or rescue result appears in the quote (abstract only), so the quote PROPOSES a pathway step rather than showing one. Per AGENT_BRIEF.md that is `hypothesis`, not `mechanism`.

to.label: Notch/Delta lateral inhibition between neighbouring non-neural ectoderm progenitors, selecting a scattered subset as multiciliated-cell precursors

lands_on.label: skin epidermis
lands_on.note: paper says 'deep layer of the non-neural ectoderm'

chain_links.experiment_type: lateral-inhibition assay by RNA injection, in situ (abstract)
chain_links.stage: non-neural ectoderm of the embryo, prior to radial intercalation

source.title: A two-step mechanism generates the spacing pattern of the ciliated cells in the skin of Xenopus embryos.

chain_links.quote: Because nascent ciliated-cell precursors prevent neighboring cells from taking on the same fate, a scattered pattern of these precursors is generated within the deep layer of the non-neural ectoderm.
chain_links.what_it_does_not_show: it gives no number: not how many multiciliated cells result, nor what fraction of the surface they cover, and nothing about a reassembled spheroid rather than an intact embryo.

chain_links.what_it_does_not_show: this quote is the fragment that survives the article's inline italic markup around 'Xenopus'; it carries the restriction of multiciliated-cell formation by Notch in Xenopus skin as prior work the paper cites, and the paper's own contribution is that mcidas is among the genes repressed by Notch. It is not a promoter-level demonstration.

downgraded_by_verification.why: The quote does not mention mcidas/MCI at all, and in context (PMC3329891.xml, first sentence of Results) it is a background citation to refs 10-13 - 'is known to be restricted by Notch signaling' - not a result of this paper. The paper's own mcidas-repressed-by-Notch finding sits in the NEXT, unquoted sentence. What the quote shows is a relation asserted from prior work, i.e. `hypothesis`.

A reagent name asserted from cited prior work is `hypothesis`, not `necessity`.

blueprint-well-formedness.label: An emitted anatomical blueprint graph is well-formed under its own rules
blueprint-well-formedness.about: the part graph itself: that each term is a node, each parent relation is one Uberon or CL relation, and the graph has no cycle
blueprint-well-formedness.how: Structural only. It certifies that the blueprint is a well-formed graph over ontology terms — it says nothing about whether the part could exist, work, or bear a load. It is the one law in the set that reaches every part of every organism, and the weakest thing anyone could want to know about any of them.

thompson1917-ch03-07.label: Weight tends to vary as the cube of linear dimensions during growth
thompson1917-ch03-07.about: the slope of log mass against log length is 3 under isometry
thompson1917-ch03-07.how: The cube law as an exponent, which makes it testable: a measured slope that is not 3 is a measurement of how the organism departs from isometry. E1 is the observation that this project's fish do depart.

altitude-coupling.label: Demand rises and supply falls with height together, so the flyable heights reach down to the ground
altitude-coupling.about: that the feasible set is downward closed in altitude: feasible high implies feasible low
altitude-coupling.how: Couples the two layers: thinner air both reduces lift and reduces oxygen, so a design feasible at altitude is feasible below it. Useful mainly as a sanity direction on a scenario sweep.

physiology-q10.label: Q10 temperature scaling: the ratio between two temperatures is Q10 raised to their difference over ten
physiology-q10.about: how a rate changes with a ten-degree change in temperature
physiology-q10.how: Proved, no instance: no candidate commits a Q10 and the conditions file fixes 25 C. Every rate in every run is therefore at one temperature, and a design whose selling point is a rate should say which temperature it means.

genotype-developmental-ordering.label: No structure develops from a precursor that appears later than it does
genotype-developmental-ordering.about: that a claimed developmental ordering has no cycle and respects the dependencies declared for it
genotype-developmental-ordering.how: The only law in the set that is about TIME, which makes it the one the time-lapse rests on. It certifies that an ordering is consistent; it does not supply one, does not predict a rate, and says nothing about how long a stage takes. A developmental animation is therefore a declared ordering being checked for consistency, never a simulation of development.

E2.label: The fitted mass exponent lies in [2.90, 3.02]
E2.about: a measured band for the weight ratio
E2.how: A measured band from one species. Outside that species it is a number, not a constraint.

E7.label: A lever lethal before the scoring stage cannot produce the phenotype
E7.about: that a trait appearing after a lethal stage cannot be scored
E7.how: The other law about time, and the one that matters most for a time-lapse: a part that appears after the organism would have died is not a part. Pairs with the developmental ordering law.

aerobic-power-bound.label: Sustained mechanical power is bounded by oxygen delivery (Fick) times efficiency
aerobic-power-bound.about: sustained flight requires aerobic supply at least the required mechanical power over the efficiency
aerobic-power-bound.how: The law that separates a glide from flight. A lifting surface large enough to hold the animal up says nothing about whether the animal can keep it up, and this is the only law in the set that asks. It takes Fick's principle as a NAMED HYPOTHESIS (fick_aerobic_supply) rather than proving it.

physiology-laplace.label: Laplace wall stress: pressure in a thin-walled vessel is limited by wall strength, thickness and radius
physiology-laplace.about: the pressure a thin-walled tube or sphere can hold, from radius, wall thickness and wall strength
physiology-laplace.how: Proved, with NO INSTANCE anywhere in this project: no vessel radius, wall thickness or wall strength exists for any organism here. It is in this table so that a part it would constrain carries the chip that says which three numbers are missing — a law with no instance is a request for data, and silence about it is worse.

muscle-power-premise.label: Thompson's muscle-power premise P = f p M (retired)
muscle-power-premise.how: STATED, NOT PROVED: a named hypothesis (MusclePowerLaw in lean/Delphi/Scaling.lean), replaced for the Studio by the aerobic bound. A chip for it must read as an assumption, because that is all it is.

fick-principle.label: Fick principle: aerobic supply is at most eta E Q (Ca - Cv)
fick-principle.about: oxygen delivery as flow times the arteriovenous difference
fick-principle.how: STATED, NOT PROVED: the aerobic bound takes it as its named hypothesis fick_aerobic_supply. Everything the aerobic bound concludes rests on it.

E3.label: Efficiency and O2 delivery lie in the ranges the cited sources support (widened after measured zebrafish)
E3.about: a measured ceiling on aerobic power
E3.how: The empirical input the aerobic bound needs. Measured in fish; borrowing it for an insect or a mammal is exactly the move the clade-scoped tables forbid.

E4.label: Gills do not ventilate in air
E4.about: a measured ceiling on stored (anaerobic) power
E4.how: The burst counterpart of E3: what a muscle can give for a few seconds. For a glide launch this is often the quantity that matters and the one least often declared.

scaling-strength-law.label: Strength scales as L^2: the missing half of Galileo's square-cube argument (R7)
scaling-strength-law.about: breaking load under isometry: it scales as L squared while weight scales as L cubed
scaling-strength-law.how: The reason a design cannot simply be made bigger. Weight grows faster than the cross-section carrying it, so a part that holds at one size fails at another with no change in material or shape.

elastic-similarity.label: Elastic similarity scaling (not formalised)
elastic-similarity.about: scaling that holds elastic deflection constant instead of stress
elastic-similarity.how: NOT FORMALISED. The named alternative to isometry for real skeletons, so its absence is why every scaling chip here says `under isometry`.

taxiing-thrust.label: Taxiing thrust on the water surface (not formalised)
taxiing-thrust.about: thrust produced while still in contact with the water
taxiing-thrust.how: NOT FORMALISED. The flying-fish runs needed it and did without it.

scaling-area-law.label: Area law and wing loading under isometry (R2, R3)
scaling-area-law.about: area under isometry: A scales as L squared
scaling-area-law.how: If the design scales a lifting or exchange surface by changing a length, this fixes the area ratio it gets — under isometry, which is a hypothesis about the design, not a fact about the animal. The flying-fish audit returns `violated` here for skin and fins, because that fish is NOT isometric: the law is right and the hypothesis is false, which is the useful outcome.

E1.label: Isometry fails within a species
E1.about: that measured fin area does not scale isometrically
E1.how: An OBSERVATION of Cypselurus hiraii, not a law. It is the evidence that the isometry hypothesis in the scaling laws is false for that fish, which is why those chips come back `violated` on that body.

genotype-pleiotropy-closure.label: An edit to a gene must be shown changing every node the map links that gene to
genotype-pleiotropy-closure.about: what a view of a genotype may omit: that the set shown is closed under the declared pleiotropy relation
genotype-pleiotropy-closure.how: A statement about the COMPLETENESS OF A VIEW, not about development. If a molecule is shown as affecting one part, this is what certifies that its other declared effects were not quietly dropped from the picture — which is exactly the failure a per-part panel invites.

genotype-genetic-code.label: A claimed amino-acid change is impossible below the code distance
genotype-genetic-code.about: what a claimed set of substitutions rules out, given the genetic code
genotype-genetic-code.how: Operates on a claimed edit. For a construct with an unedited donor genome there is nothing for it to operate on, and that is the honest answer rather than a refusal.

gene-regulatory-dynamics.label: Gene regulatory dynamics (not formalised)
gene-regulatory-dynamics.about: the dynamics of a regulatory network
gene-regulatory-dynamics.how: NOT FORMALISED, and it is the hole the whole scale ladder sits over. Nothing in the Lean set connects a molecule to a tissue. The ladder's molecular rungs are therefore LITERATURE, graded and quoted, and the theatre must never draw them in the same colour as a proof.

universal_laws.because: the quantities are there and no check in this run evaluated this law against them
scope.taxa is [Danio rerio], and Xenopus laevis (donor) is in none of them. Its numbers are another clade's.

missing_rungs.why: A xenobot has no organ. Kriegman et al. 2020 say so of their own constructs: 'above the cellular level, they bear little resemblance to existing organs or organisms' (runs/_chains/raw/xenobot/PMC6994979.xml, byte-exact). Links l12 and l13 therefore step straight from tissue to phenotype with skipped_rung set to 'organ'.
missing_rungs.what_would_be_needed: Nothing can close this one by experiment: the rung does not exist in this organism. A viewer that insists on an organ layer should render it as explicitly empty rather than invent one.

missing_rungs.why: No document fetched in this run gives a xenobot locomotion speed in any unit, so the requirement's 0.5-1 mm/s figure is unsourced as far as this ladder is concerned. The paper that reports ciliary xenobot locomotion quantitatively, Blackiston et al. 2021 Science Robotics, is not open access: its abstract was readable through PubMed, but Europe PMC returned HTTP 404 for its full text because it has no PMCID.
missing_rungs.what_would_be_needed: The full text or supplementary movies of Blackiston et al. 2021 (doi 10.1126/scirobotics.abf1571), or any tracked-trajectory dataset of ciliated xenobots with a calibrated scale bar and frame rate.

missing_rungs.why: Nothing fetched links a MEASURED multiciliated-cell density or coverage on a xenobot to that xenobot's measured speed or to how many particles it moves. Boselli et al. 2021 model coverage against transport on a flat Xenopus epidermis; Kriegman et al. 2021 observe locomotion and piling on a spheroid; no document connects the two quantities in the same specimen.
missing_rungs.what_would_be_needed: Per-xenobot multiciliated-cell counts (acetylated-tubulin staining, say) paired with tracked speed and a per-organism count of particles displaced, across a range of Notch-ICD doses.

missing_rungs.why: There is no genotype variable in this organism at all: the donor genome is unedited. The only molecular handles found in anything fetched here are an injected mRNA (Notch ICD, l14, which REMOVES ciliary locomotion) and a drug (WNT3A, l15, in a different Xenopus species and in an intact embryo). No document shows any molecular manipulation that INCREASES xenobot speed or improves particle sweeping.
missing_rungs.what_would_be_needed: A xenobot built from cells injected with mcidas or foxj1 mRNA (to raise multiciliated-cell number), or treated with WNT3A, with speed and particle sweeping measured against uninjected controls in the same dish.

missing_rungs.why: The serotonin/Htr3 beat-frequency loop (l09, l10) was shown in tadpole skin. Nothing fetched shows that small secretory cells exist in a xenobot at all, so it is unknown whether this control loop is present in the construct.
missing_rungs.what_would_be_needed: An in situ or scRNA-seq census of a mature xenobot for small-secretory-cell markers. The Lee et al. 2023 animal-cap organoid atlas is the closest available dataset and does profile ionocytes and goblet cells, but the xenobot itself was not checked here.

missing_rungs.why: ADDED BY VERIFICATION. l03 is the only link joining the Notch/Delta lateral-inhibition arm (l01, l02) to the multicilin arm (l04-l07), and its quote does not name mcidas and is a background citation rather than a result of the paper it is drawn from (see l03.downgraded_by_verification). With l03 at hypothesis grade, the two molecular arms of this ladder are not experimentally joined by anything fetched here: there is no quoted evidence that Notch represses mcidas specifically.
missing_rungs.what_would_be_needed: A quotable result sentence or figure legend from Stubbs et al. 2012 or a successor showing mcidas transcript or reporter levels rising when Notch activity is lowered and falling when it is raised, in the same experiment.

missing_rungs.why: ADDED BY VERIFICATION. A specimen break, distinct from the quantitative gap already logged between cell_cell and tissue. Every link from molecule through cell_cell (l01-l10) is evidenced in an intact Xenopus embryo or in an animal-cap explant; the only links whose organism_of_evidence is a xenobot are l11, l12, l13 - all `association`, all purely observational - and l14, now `hypothesis`. So no fetched document shows ANY of the Notch, multicilin or serotonin steps actually operating inside a reassembled spheroid: the mechanistic upper half of the ladder and the xenobot phenotype are joined by inference, not by a shared specimen.
missing_rungs.what_would_be_needed: In situ, immunostaining or scRNA-seq on mature xenobots for X-Delta-1/Notch targets, mcidas, foxj1 and acetylated tubulin, showing the same programme runs in the construct; ideally with a Notch-ICD dose series scored in the spheroid itself.

verification.stance: Every claim was re-derived from the bytes. Quote matching was done by script, not by eye.

method.quote_matching: Python: each `quote` normalised to single spaces and searched in (a) the raw file, (b) the file with XML tags deleted (zero-width tag boundary), (c) the file with tags replaced by a space. A quote counted as verified only on a literal substring hit.
method.fetch_log: Each distinct `quote_from` path matched against runs/_chains/log/xenobot.fetch.json by `saved_to`, status asserted 200, and the file's sha256 recomputed and compared with the logged digest.
method.citation_identity: The pmid and doi claimed in each link's `source` compared with the pmid and doi recorded inside the fetched document.
method.grades: Each `evidence_grade` re-read against the five definitions in genotype/AGENT_BRIEF.md, judged strictly on what the QUOTE shows, not on what the paper as a whole probably shows.
method.holdout: Scanned for the names and terms of the held-out clade; no source from it was used in any link, quote or evidence field. The scan itself is in the fetch log and the verifier's scripts, not restated here.
method.identifiers: All 32 logged URLs parsed: hosts, query-parameter names, plus a regex scan of the entire log for email addresses, personal names, account ids, api keys and NCBI tool=/email= parameters.

results.walkable: The ladder IS walkable end to end as topology: molecule->pathway (l04 necessity, l05 mechanism), pathway->cell (l06 sufficiency), cell->cell_cell (l09 necessity), cell_cell->tissue (l10 necessity, l08 hypothesis), then tissue->phenotype directly (l12, l13 association) because the organ rung does not exist in this organism. Two of the three downgrades, l01 and l03, fall on the Notch/Delta arm, which is a parallel entry into the pathway rung, so none of them severs the walkable path. The path is nonetheless carried across its final step by `association`-grade observation only, and its mechanistic rungs come from a different specimen than its phenotype rungs - see the two missing_rungs added by this verification.

cell<->tissue: specimen break - no fetched document shows the mechanistic rungs operating inside a xenobot
results.holdout: Scanned for the names and terms of the held-out clade; no source from it was used in any link, quote or evidence field. The scan itself is in the fetch log and the verifier's scripts, not restated here.
results.identifier_leak: NONE. 32 logged URLs across 4 hosts (www.ebi.ac.uk, eutils.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov, rest.uniprot.org, ubergraph.apps.renci.org); query parameters are only db, fields, format, id, pageSize, query, resultType, retmode, rettype, size. No email address, personal name, account id, api key, or NCBI tool=/email= parameter anywhere in the log.

checks.body: The answer changes inside the stated ranges: 0.132x the force needed at the worst corner and 13.236x at the best. Narrow an input and ask again.

numbers.model: Stokes drag, F = 6*pi*mu*a*v. Exact for a sphere in the creeping limit.
numbers.model_caveat: Drag on an isolated sphere in an unbounded fluid. A particle resting on a surface also has friction and adhesion, which are often LARGER than the drag and are not modelled here; particles in a pile shield one another, which this does not model either; and a non-spherical particle has a different coefficient. Treat the force here as a lower bound on what the task needs.
cannot_say: whether the design can GET to the particle, aim at it, or hold on to it: there is no control model
whether a pile forms: moving particles and accumulating them are different problems, and the second is about where they are released
how long it would take, or whether the organism can pay for it

checks.body: At every corner of the stated ranges the declared thrust exceeds the drag: 5.00e-10 N against the 3.78e-10 N needed to move 2 particles of radius 0.00001-0.00005 m at 0.0002 m/s through water. Margin 1.324x to 13.236x. The design did not get stronger between these two calls: the CLAIM got narrower, from twenty particles at once to two. That is the loop working as intended -- the check named the corner that failed, and the honest response was to stop claiming that corner.
